title: Riverhog provenance journal entry
description: Path-independent opaque-artifact provenance. Hard-cut current contract; package and wire versions are unchanged.

time.description: UTC instant, no leap-second spellings; calendar validity and nanosecond ordering are application constraints.

json.description: Null-free portable JSON; exact fractional or wider numeric values use typed decimal/integer strings. No floats in opaque profile JSON.

content.description: Only the bounded primary byte sequence. Native streams, forks, attributes and metadata do not enter this digest.

externalReference.description: A reference to an exact assertion in an immutable foreign entry. It does not import or independently authenticate that assertion.

byteName.description: Exact source units, including non-Unicode path or name sequences. Display text is never identity.

intervalExtent.description: Known bounds only, [start,end) when both exist. Omitted bound is unknown, not infinity.

artifact.description: Governed continuity identity, not a path or digest and not an automatic PROV specialization assertion.

occurrence.description: A contextual instance/exposure. Membership is an attributed continuity judgment; multiple retained replicas have distinct occurrence identities. materialization_hint is optional descriptive advice under this occurrence assertion, not a fixed identity aspect; corrections use normal assertion retraction/replacement.

state.description: Fixed aspects of an occurrence. Descriptions carry observed or reported values; addresses do not define state identity.

agent.description: A responsible agent. A host or service is not automatically an agent.

context.description: A described context, not necessarily a physical host. Source, execution and recordkeeping are independent activity roles.

observation.description: An immutable observation record generated by capture, not the observed state itself. Direct primary-content measurement requires complete size/SHA-256.

reportedDescription.description: A historical or imported assertion. Missing content, source location, context or generation event remains unknown; no synthetic capture is required.

invalidation.description: Invalidates only the specified occurrence state, not its artifact, replicas or provenance records.

specialization.description: Explicit PROV specialization claim; never inferred from lineage membership, paths or fixity.

continuity.description: An attributed continuity judgment, not necessarily a change or a derivation.

comparison.description: Comparison of cited primary-content descriptions only. Matching digests do not establish identity, direction or metadata equality.

locatorBinding.description: Optional, plural, contextual designation. Missing interval endpoints do not imply perpetual validity; no global current-path register exists.

locatorBindingEnd.description: Evidence that one specifically identified binding ceased. It does not invalidate the payload or other aliases.

deliveryAssociation.description: Association to a supplied payload slot within a delivery instance; the slot is opaque, not a path. Verifies primary bytes, not every native attribute.

availabilityAssertion.description: Availability is scoped to an occurrence. Absence of a locator or a successful destination copy is not proof of source removal.

journalSubject.description: What a journal describes, independent of where the journal or payload is stored.

extension.description: Attributed URI-named extension. Does not override the core and must not interpret primary media/document bytes in this profile.

graphFragment.description: Atomic sets of attributable assertions. Array and append order imply neither causality nor event chronology.

correctionBody.description: Monotonic retraction of specific prior assertions, with optional atomic replacements bearing new assertion IDs. Does not denote artifact change or reactivate retracted assertions.

materializationHint.description: Optional attributed recommendation for human-facing materialization, not identity, an observed locator, an authoritative destination or a source relationship. Components are ordered relative Unicode labels; consumers validate and escape for their actual destination. No case or Unicode normalization is implied.
